desc:
Custom BigCommerce app development adds the one feature your store needs when no marketplace app fits. Ecom Swift LLC builds storefront scripts and private apps on the official BigCommerce APIs, tests them on a sandbox store, and installs them in your own account.

## What is a custom BigCommerce app?

A custom BigCommerce app is a small piece of software that adds a feature your store does not have out of the box. It talks to your store through the official APIs and webhooks, or it runs as a script on your storefront pages. Some are private apps that only your store uses. Others are tiny scripts that change how one page behaves.

Typical examples are a delivery date picker at checkout, a product add-on field such as engraving text, a rule that blocks certain product combinations, or a nightly sync between your catalog and a spreadsheet. If you can describe the rule in one or two sentences, it can usually be built.

## Why a marketplace app is sometimes not enough

Marketplace apps are written for the average store. When your process is different, you end up paying for a large tool that does a tenth of what you need, or you work around its gaps by hand. Each extra app also adds code to your pages and another monthly bill.

A custom build does exactly one job and nothing else. That keeps your storefront lighter, your admin simpler and your team out of copy-and-paste routines. It also means the feature behaves the way your business works, not the way a vendor guessed it might.

## How a custom app changes your results

The value comes from removing friction in two places. On the storefront, a well-placed feature such as a date picker or an add-on field answers a question the shopper would otherwise email you about, so fewer carts stall. Behind the scenes, an automated rule replaces manual checking, so orders move faster and mistakes drop.

Because the app is built around your catalog and your workflow, it also avoids the clutter that generic tools bring. Pages stay quicker, and the feature is easier to maintain. Results still depend on your products and traffic, so we describe what the feature does, not what it will earn.

## What a well-built BigCommerce app includes

- A clear written scope: what the feature does, what triggers it and what it must never do.
- Use of official BigCommerce APIs and webhooks rather than fragile workarounds.
- API credentials limited to the exact permissions the feature needs.
- Testing on a sandbox store before anything touches your live catalog.
- Error logging, so a failed call is recorded instead of silently lost.
- A settings screen where you can change values without editing code.
- Storefront scripts added through the platform's own script tools, so they can be switched off in one click.
- Hosting and data storage that fit the size of the job.
- A short usage note that explains setup, behavior and what to do if something looks wrong.

## How we build it

We start with a short call or message thread to pin down the rule, the trigger and the edge cases. Then we choose the lightest approach. A small job becomes a storefront script. A larger one becomes a private app with its own settings screen.

We build and test on a sandbox store with sample products and orders. When the behavior is right, we install it in your own store and watch the first real events. The Basic package covers one script or small API task, Standard covers a private app with one core feature and a settings screen, and Premium covers several features with hosting, automated tests and the source code handed over.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the problem in plain words, including who triggers it and what should happen.
- Share examples of real orders or products where the current process breaks.
- Keep the first version small, then add features once it works.
- Decide who on your team will manage the settings screen.
- Ask for the source code and notes so you are never locked in.

**Avoid:**
- Installing a heavy marketplace app for a single small feature.
- Giving an app wider API permissions than it needs.
- Testing directly on your live catalog.
- Adding rules that conflict with your theme or existing apps without checking.
- Leaving a custom feature undocumented, so nobody knows how it works later.

## Who this is for

This service suits a store owner whose product needs a custom field that no theme supports, an operations manager tired of retyping orders into another system, and a growing brand that wants one tailored rule instead of three overlapping apps. It also suits agencies that need a reliable builder for a client request.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of the feature, a few examples of how it should behave, and any tool it must connect to. We never need your password. Instead, you add us as a limited user in your store, and we use a scoped API account for the app itself, which you can revoke at any time. We confirm the plan in writing before building.
